mainTopic: Sending items on יום טוב (כלאים fabrics, shoes, תפילין) and what to do with תפילין when the holy day begins.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how the משנה can allow sending כלאים garments on יום טוב: it means hard fabrics like felt. רב פפא, רבא and רב אשי then discuss felt socks, coin bundles and seed pouches. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's list of shoes. A סנדל המסומר may not be worn because of a past tragedy, but אביי proves from the משנה's wording that it may be moved. An unsewn shoe may not be sent even if it is pinned together. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי only seem to argue about white and black shoes, since each followed how shoes were made in his town. The משנה's general rule is read to allow sending anything usable on a weekday, so רב ששת permits sending תפילין. אביי then teaches what to do if one is still wearing תפילין when the holy day begins. The גמרא settles the clash with a ברייתא and a משנה by sorting out how safe the תפילין are from dogs and thieves. The chapter ends with the הדרן.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about hard fabrics
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the כלאים garments the משנה allows sending are hard ones. It supports this with רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's ruling that hard felt from נרש is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה means hard garments. This fits what רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: this hard felt made in נרש is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering the earlier question of what use a כלאים garment has on יום טוב. It says the משנה means hard fabric, which may be used even though it is כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא could not find a permitted use for a כלאים garment. The new idea is that hard, stiff material is not treated as a normal garment for כלאים, so one may sit on it. רב הונא's ruling about felt from נרש shows this is an accepted rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixture, here wool and linen together (שעטנז)

phrases.english: Rather, it means hard ones,
phrases.notes: He means hard garments, which may be used even if they are כלאים.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: and like what Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
this hard felt of Neresh is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous section about what use a כלאים garment could have on יום טוב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה refers only to hard fabrics.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have thought any כלאים garment is forbidden to use, so sending it would serve no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hard fabrics like felt have no כלאים problem for sitting on, so sending them is useful and allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hard felt from נרש is permitted despite being כלאים.

steps.title: Felt socks have no כלאים problem
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that felt socks are not subject to כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: felt socks do not have a כלאים problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds another example of a hard item that is free from כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the rule just stated about hard fabric. Even though socks are worn on the body, felt socks are stiff, so they are treated like hard felt and are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not fall under (a prohibition)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
felt socks — there is no prohibition of diverse kinds in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another example of the hard-fabric rule from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Felt socks are not subject to כלאים.

steps.title: רבא: coin bundles are allowed, seed pouches are not
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that hard coin bundles have no כלאים problem, but pouches used for seeds do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: these coin bundles have no כלאים problem. But seed pouches do have a כלאים problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא names two kinds of small bags and draws a line between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coin bundles are hard, so they fit the rule from step 1 and are allowed. Seed pouches are bigger and softer, so רבא says they are treated like real cloth and כלאים applies.

phrases.english: Rava said:
these bundles for coins —
there is no prohibition of diverse kinds in them;
those for seeds — there is a prohibition of diverse kinds in them.
phrases.notes: The word for bundles carries over: he means the bags used for holding seeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases, including one where כלאים does apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coin bundles are free from כלאים; seed pouches are subject to כלאים.

steps.title: רב אשי: both kinds of bags are allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees with רבא and allows both coin bundles and seed pouches, since people do not use them to keep warm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: both this one and that one have no כלאים problem, because this is not a way of keeping warm.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with רבא and permits the seed pouches too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא looked at whether the material is hard or soft. רב אשי uses a different test: כלאים applies to things that warm the body like clothing, and bags are not used that way. So even soft seed pouches are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: Hard fabrics like felt are not a problem for כלאים. רבא forbids soft seed pouches, but רב אשי allows all such bags because they are not used for warmth.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
both this and that
have no prohibition of diverse kinds in them,
because this is not a way of keeping warm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבא's ruling on seed pouches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bags of any kind are free from כלאים because they are not used for warmth.

steps.title: Why is a spiked sandal not allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'but not a סנדל המסומר' and asks the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but not a spiked sandal. Why is a spiked sandal not allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and asks why a spiked sandal is excluded. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sandal is a normal item, so it is not clear why it would be worse than other things one may send. The גמרא wants the source of this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A sandal with nails or spikes in the sole

phrases.english: But not a spiked sandal.
A spiked sandal — what is the reason it is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כלאים topic and opens the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a סנדל המסומר may not be sent or worn.

steps.title: Because of a past tragedy
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ban comes from an incident that once happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of an incident that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים made this rule because of a sad event in the past.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is not because the sandal itself is a forbidden item. It is a גזירה made after a tragedy that happened when people wore these sandals, so the חכמים forbade wearing them on שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: Because of an incident that occurred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is a rabbinic decree made because of a past incident.

steps.title: אביי: you may not wear it, but you may move it
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that a סנדל המסומר may not be worn but may be moved. Wearing is forbidden because of the incident.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: a spiked sandal may not be worn but may be moved. It may not be worn because of the incident that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי splits the rule into two parts: wearing is forbidden, moving is allowed. He explains the first part here and proves the second part in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree targeted wearing the sandal, since the tragedy came from wearing. אביי holds that the decree does not make the sandal מוקצה, so carrying it around is still fine.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up wearing and moving. A ban on wearing something does not automatically make it forbidden to pick up.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
a spiked sandal is forbidden to wear
and permitted to move.
Forbidden to wear — because of the incident that occurred,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: סַנְדָּל הַמְסוּמָּר אָסוּר לְנׇעֳלוֹ וּמוּתָּר לְטַלְטְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reason from step 6 and adds that moving is allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סנדל המסומר may not be worn but may be moved.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's wording that moving is allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves moving is allowed: if it were forbidden even to move, the משנה would not need to say you may not send it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted to move it, as we see from the משנה saying 'one may not send.' If you thought it was forbidden to move it, then since even moving is forbidden, would we need to be told that sending is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reads the משנה closely to prove the second half of his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sending something means carrying it, which is more than just moving it. If moving were already forbidden, sending would obviously be forbidden too, and the משנה would not bother to say so. Since the משנה does say 'one may not send,' moving itself must be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it teaches

steps.whatToRemember: A סנדל המסומר: wearing is forbidden because of a past tragedy, but moving it is allowed. אביי proves this from the משנה's need to say 'one may not send.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool: if a משנה states something, it must not be obvious, and from that we learn what the משנה must hold.

phrases.english: and permitted to move —
from the fact that it teaches: 'One may not send,'
for if it entered your mind that it is forbidden to move it,
now, if even moving it is forbidden,
is sending it necessary to state?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half of אביי's ruling from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That a סנדל המסומר may be moved.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'אין משלחין', which would be unneeded if moving were forbidden.

steps.title: Why would the משנה need to forbid an unsewn shoe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on sending an unsewn shoe and asks why this needs saying, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And not a shoe that is not sewn.' That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה's list and objects that it seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only things a person can use may be sent on יום טוב. An unsewn shoe can't be worn, so of course it can't be sent. The objection is that the משנה seems to be teaching something we already know.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (an objection that the text says something unnecessary)

phrases.english: And not a shoe that is not sewn.
That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the סנדל המסומר to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words 'ולא מנעל שאינו תפור'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unsewn shoe can't be used, so it obviously can't be sent. The משנה's statement looks unnecessary.

steps.title: The case is a shoe held together with pins
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a shoe held together with pins, which could be worn but still may not be sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed only to teach that even though it is held together with pins, it still may not be sent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is teaching about a shoe pinned together, which you might have thought counts as usable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pinned shoe can actually be worn, so we might think it is allowed to be sent. The משנה teaches that it still counts as an unsewn shoe, so it may not be sent.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for... (introduces a less obvious case)

phrases.english: It was needed only
for when, even though it is held together with pins, it still may not be sent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' objection by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A pinned shoe can be worn, so maybe it may be sent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a pinned shoe counts as unsewn and may not be sent.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids sending a white shoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה and brings a ברייתא: he allows a black shoe but forbids a white one, because it still needs chalk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יהודה says, not even a white shoe. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה allows a black shoe and forbids a white one, because it still needs a lump of chalk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's words in the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A white shoe is not ready to wear until it is whitened with chalk. Since it is not yet usable, it may not be sent on יום טוב. A black shoe is already finished, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Not even a white shoe.
It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda permits a black one,
and forbids a white one,
because it needs a lump of chalk.
phrases.notes: The chalk was used to whiten the shoe, so it isn't ready to wear yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף לֹא מִנְעָל לָבָן. תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה and supports it with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a black shoe may be sent and a white one may not, because a white one still needs chalk.

steps.title: רבי יוסי forbids sending a black shoe
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי says the opposite: a black shoe is forbidden because it still needs polishing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי forbids a black shoe, because it needs to be polished.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי's view, which seems to be the exact opposite of רבי יהודה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the black shoe is the unfinished one, since it still needs polishing. So the two תנאים seem to argue about which color shoe is ready to wear. This sets up the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei forbids a black one,
because it needs to be polished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: a black shoe may not be sent, because it still needs polishing.

steps.title: They don't really argue; each followed his own town
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי agree on the rule. Shoes were made differently in each of their towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: They don't really disagree. Each Sage spoke about his own place. In one Sage's place, the flesh side of the leather faced down. In the other Sage's place, the flesh side faced up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the apparent argument by saying each תנא was describing how shoes were made where he lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the rule: a shoe that still needs work may not be sent. The only difference was the local way of making shoes. Where the rough flesh side of the hide faced outward, black shoes needed polishing. Where it faced inward, they didn't.

keyTerms.meaning: Each Sage according to his own place
The flesh side of the hide

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי share one rule: an unfinished shoe can't be sent. Their different rulings come only from how shoes were made in their towns.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree.
This Sage ruled according to his place,
and that Sage ruled according to his place.
In the place of this Sage, the flesh side faced down,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה's town. The rough flesh side faced the inside of the shoe, so no polishing was needed.

phrases.english: in the place of that Sage, the flesh side faced up.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי's town. The rough side faced outward, so it needed polishing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי. מָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ וּמָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent argument between steps 11 and 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different local realities, not a real argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two תנאים argue about which color shoe may be sent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree that a shoe needing more work can't be sent. Local shoemaking decided which color needed work.

steps.title: רב ששת allows sending תפילין on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general rule, then reports that רב ששת allowed the רבנן to send תפילין on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: This is the rule: anything one may use on יום טוב may be sent. רב ששת allowed the רבנן to send תפילין on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general rule and brings רב ששת's ruling allowing תפילין to be sent. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since תפילין are not worn on יום טוב, רב ששת's ruling seems to clash with the משנה's rule as it is worded. The גמרא puts the two side by side to prepare the next move.

phrases.english: This is the rule:
anything that one may use on a Festival.
Rav Sheshet permitted the Sages
to send tefillin on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל כֹּל שֶׁנֵּאוֹתִין בּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the משנה's closing general rule and an אמורא's practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת: תפילין may be sent on יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי challenges רב ששת from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the משנה only allows sending things usable on יום טוב, and תפילין are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But didn't we learn in the משנה that anything one may use on יום טוב may be sent? (תפילין aren't worn on יום טוב.)
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב ששת's ruling using the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties sending to being usable on יום טוב itself. תפילין are not worn on יום טוב, so they should not be allowed to be sent.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But didn't we learn:
anything that one may use on a Festival,
one may send it!
phrases.notes: The point he leaves unsaid: תפילין aren't worn on יום טוב, so how can they be sent?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's ruling from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's permission to send תפילין on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows sending only what is usable on יום טוב. תפילין are not used on יום טוב.

steps.title: The rule means usable on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה: anything usable on a weekday may be sent on יום טוב, so תפילין are fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: anything one may use on a weekday may be sent on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by explaining the משנה's rule in a new way, which supports רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בְּיוֹם טוֹב' in the rule describe when the sending happens, not when the item is used. As long as the item is useful on a regular weekday, it may be sent on יום טוב. תפילין are used on weekdays, so they may be sent.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereading a text)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule is: anything usable on a weekday may be sent on יום טוב. That is why תפילין may be sent.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the rule as 'only things used on יום טוב.' The words 'on יום טוב' tell you when the sending happens, not when the item is used.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading makes the sending rule much broader. It includes items like תפילין that are useful in general but not on יום טוב itself.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
anything that one may use on a weekday,
one may send it on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge and defends רב ששת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only items usable on יום טוב itself may be sent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Items usable on a weekday may be sent on יום טוב, so תפילין are allowed.

steps.title: אביי: Cover the תפילין with your hand until you get home
steps.stepSummary: אביי teaches that someone still wearing תפילין when שבת or יום טוב begins covers them with his hand and walks home with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Since we are talking about תפילין, let us teach something about them. If a person was traveling with תפילין on his head and the sun set, he puts his hand over them until he reaches his house. If he was sitting in the בית המדרש with תפילין on his head and the holy day began, he puts his hand over them until he reaches his house.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses the earlier talk about sending תפילין as a chance to teach a new law about them. He says that a person caught wearing תפילין when the holy day starts covers them and keeps going until he gets home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a person who was wearing תפילין during the day and was still wearing them when שבת or יום טוב began. אביי rules that he does not have to take them off right away. He covers them with his hand and walks all the way to his own house, whether he was on the road or in the בית המדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: Since they have come to our hands, meaning since this topic came up
The sun set while he was still on the way
The holy day began while he was there
He places his hand over them to cover them

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. It is not about sending תפילין as a gift, as in the last steps. It is about a person who is still wearing them when the holy day starts.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Tefillin, since they have come to our hands,
phrases.notes: He means: since we just talked about תפילין in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: let us say a matter about them:
If one was coming on the road
and tefillin were on his head,
and the sun set upon him
he places his hand upon them
until he reaches his house.
If he was sitting in the study hall
and tefillin were on his head
and the day became holy upon him
he places his hand upon them
until he reaches his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי תפילין הואיל ואתו לידן נימא בהו מילתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the mention of תפילין in Steps 14-16 to open a new, related topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One caught wearing תפילין as שבת or יום טוב begins covers them with his hand and continues until he reaches his own house.

steps.title: A ברייתא says only to the nearest house
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב איקא cites a ברייתא that says he walks only to the house closest to the city wall or to the בית המדרש, not all the way home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב איקא, objected from a ברייתא: If a person was traveling with תפילין on his head and the holy day began, he covers them with his hand until he reaches the house nearest the city wall. If he was sitting in the בית המדרש and the holy day began, he covers them until he reaches the house nearest the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב איקא challenges אביי with a ברייתא. The ברייתא gives a shorter limit: only to the nearest house, not to his own home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the person may go all the way to his own house. The ברייתא says he stops at the first house he reaches, near the wall or near the בית המדרש. So the two sources seem to disagree on how far he may go.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
The house nearest the city wall
The house nearest the study hall

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Ika raised an objection:
If one was coming on the road
and tefillin were on his head
and the day became holy upon him
he places his hand upon them
until he reaches the house nearest the wall.
If he was sitting in the study hall
and the day became holy upon him
he places his hand upon them

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַבַּיִת הַסָּמוּךְ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
phrases.english: until he reaches the house nearest the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתיב רב הונא בריה דרב איקא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's ruling in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that one may walk with the covered תפילין all the way to his own house.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא limits the walk to the nearest house, which seems to contradict אביי's longer limit.

steps.title: Guarded versus not guarded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about where the תפילין can be safely guarded in the nearest house. אביי is talking about where they cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a difficulty. This source is where the תפילין are guarded, and that source is where they are not guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. It says the two sources are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the nearest house is a safe place to leave the תפילין, he stops there, as the ברייתא says. If it is not safe, he may keep going all the way home, as אביי says. So the sources do not really argue.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a difficulty; the sources are talking about different cases

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where they are guarded,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא of רב הונא: the nearest house is a safe place to leave them.

phrases.english: that is where they are not guarded.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא קשיא הא דמנטרא הא דלא מנטרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 18 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source deals with a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי and the ברייתא disagree about how far one may walk with the תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is where the nearest house can guard them; אביי is where it cannot, so he may continue home.

steps.title: Then why must they be on his head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the case is where the תפילין are not guarded, why does it matter that they were on his head? Even תפילין found on the ground may be brought in.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the case is where they are not guarded, why talk specifically about תפילין on his head? Even if they were lying on the ground, the same should be true, for we learned in a משנה: One who finds תפילין brings them in one pair at a time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It argues that if the reason is that the תפילין are not guarded, the detail 'on his head' should not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה already teaches that someone who finds unguarded תפילין on the ground may bring them in by wearing them, one pair at a time. So if אביי's case is only about unguarded תפילין, there was no need to say they were already on his head. That detail now looks pointless, which weakens the answer of Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? Why mention this detail?

phrases.english: If it is where they are not guarded,
why specifically on his head?
Even if they are lying on the ground, also,
for we have learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in עירובין 95a.

phrases.english: One who finds tefillin brings them in pair by pair!
phrases.notes: He brings them in by wearing them, one pair at a time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אי דלא מנטרא מאי איריא בראשו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 19 that אביי's case is about unguarded תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is that the תפילין are unguarded, the detail 'on his head' adds nothing. A משנה already allows bringing in unguarded תפילין found on the ground.

steps.title: Safe from thieves and dogs versus safe only from dogs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא separates two levels of danger. In אביי's case (תפילין on his head, brought all the way home), the תפילין are safe from thieves and from dogs. In the משנה about finding תפילין, they are safe from dogs but not from thieves.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. אביי's case is talking about a place where the תפילין are guarded from both thieves and dogs. The משנה is talking about a place where they are guarded from dogs but not from thieves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20 by describing two different situations, each with its own level of danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תפילין are safe from both thieves and dogs, only a person already wearing them takes them along, and תפילין lying on the ground are left. This matches אביי's case, which speaks of תפילין on his head. If thieves could still take them, the danger is greater, so even תפילין lying on the ground are brought in, as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer that shows two sources do not really clash.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. אביי's case of תפילין on his head has the safer situation (safe from both). The משנה about finding תפילין has the riskier one (thieves are still a danger).

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is where they are guarded from thieves
phrases.notes: "This one" is אביי's teaching from step 17, about a person who already has the תפילין on his head.

phrases.english: and from dogs.
That one is where they are guarded from dogs
phrases.notes: "That one" is the משנה from step 20, about finding תפילין on the ground.

phrases.english: but not guarded from thieves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by setting up two levels of protection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source deals with a different level of danger.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי's case and the משנה seem to deal with the same unguarded case, so the 'on his head' detail seems pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי's case covers a situation safe from thieves and dogs, so only תפילין already on his head are taken along. The משנה covers a case safe only from dogs, where thieves are still a risk.

steps.title: Even Jewish thieves are a concern
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the חידוש of the משנה. You might think that most bandits are Jews who would not disrespect תפילין, so there is nothing to fear. The משנה teaches that we still worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: most bandits are Jews, and they would not treat תפילין with disrespect, so there is no need to bring them in. The משנה teaches us that we still bring them in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what new thing the משנה teaches in the case where the תפילין are not safe from thieves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could argue that thieves are no real danger, since most of them are Jews who would treat stolen תפילין with respect. The משנה rejects this. It still tells us to bring the תפילין in, because some thieves might not respect them.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. This introduces a mistaken thought that the source comes to correct.
It teaches us. This introduces the חידוש, the new point of the source.

steps.whatToRemember: In אביי's case (safe from thieves and dogs), only תפילין already on one's head are taken along. The משנה (thieves still a risk) requires bringing in even תפילין found on the ground. We worry even though most thieves are Jews.

phrases.english: You might have said:
most bandits are Jews
and they would not treat them with disrespect,
so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה. It still tells us to bring the תפילין in, even with Jewish thieves around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the חידוש of the משנה in the case step 21 set up (not safe from thieves).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה requires bringing in found תפילין where thieves are a danger, even though most bandits are Jews who would probably respect them.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter ביצה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line for the first chapter of the מסכת, פרק ביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק ביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the chapter ביצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is said when finishing a chapter. It expresses the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of the first chapter, taken from its opening word.

phrases.english: We will return to you, ביצה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion about תפילין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the first chapter, פרק ביצה.
